title: How to insert a table in Keynote on Mac: step by step for Keynote 15.4
metaTitle: How to insert a table in Keynote on Mac (step by step)
description: How to insert a table in Keynote on Mac: click Insert Table or Chart, choose Tables, pick a layout, then type in the cells. Steps for Keynote 15.4.

intro: To insert a table in Keynote on Mac, open your presentation, select the slide, and click the Insert Table or Chart button in the toolbar. Then click Tables, pick a layout in the Add Table pane, and either select it or drag it onto the slide.
tldr: Click Insert Table or Chart in the toolbar, then click Tables.
Pick a layout in the Add Table pane, or drag one onto the slide.
Click a cell to type. Drag the Table handle in the top-left corner to move the table.
If the table will not change, it may be locked. The Arrange menu can reverse that.

blocks.text: Check your Keynote version first

Keynote on Mac has changed its toolbar over the years, so start by checking your version. Apple's current Mac guide covers Keynote 15.4, and it calls the toolbar button Insert Table or Chart. Apple's older guide for Keynote 13.1 calls the same button simply Table.

To check, choose Keynote > About Keynote. The App Store listing shows version 15.4.2 and says it requires macOS 26.0 or later. TidBITS reported that Keynote 15.4 raised the system requirement to macOS 26 Tahoe. If your Mac runs an older system, you cannot install the current version, so the steps here may not match your screen.
Pick a layout in the Add Table pane

After you click Insert Table or Chart, click Tables. The Add Table pane opens with left and right arrows. Use them to browse the layouts before you pick one. Compare a few designs first, because the pane is the only place to see them side by side.

You have two ways to place the table. Select a layout and it appears on the slide. Or drag the layout from the pane onto the slide and drop it where you want it. Dragging is quicker when you already know the position, because it skips a move later.
Pick the layout closest to your data. Rows and columns can be added or removed later, so an exact count is not required before you start.
Type in cells and edit the text

Click an empty cell and start typing. To change text that is already in a cell, double-click it so the insertion point lands where you click. Pressing Delete clears the contents of a selected cell and leaves the cell in place.

Apple's guide also covers wrapping. Control-click a cell and choose Wrap Text to make long entries wrap inside the cell. Edit > Clear All removes the text and the formatting, which is a different result from Delete.
If your typing goes nowhere, check two things. Make sure you clicked inside a cell, not the slide around the table. Then check whether the table is locked, which is covered further down.
Move, resize and delete the table

Keynote treats the whole table as one object, and the Table handle is how you grab it. Click the table and find the handle in its top-left corner. Drag that handle to move the table anywhere on the slide. Move it before you resize it, so you know where the edges will land.

To resize, click the table, click the Table handle, and drag the white square in the bottom-right corner. Hold Shift while you drag to keep the proportions. Without Shift, the width and height change separately, and the table can stretch out of shape.

blocks.title: Cell or table?
blocks.text: Clicking a single cell and pressing Delete clears the text in that cell. It does not remove the table. Select the table itself and click the Table handle first.
To delete the whole table, click it, click the Table handle, and press Delete. The rest of the slide stays as it was.
Add and remove rows and columns

Table size is the thing people change most often. Keynote's shortcuts work on the cells you have selected. Hold Option and press an arrow key to add a row or column next to those cells. Option-Return adds a row at the bottom of the table.
Tab works at the right edge. When the cursor is in the rightmost column, Tab inserts a new column on the right. That is useful when you type across a table and run out of room.
To remove rows or columns, select them and press Option-Command-Delete for rows or Control-Command-Delete for columns. Control-click also offers Delete Rows and Delete Columns in its menu.
A worked example: building a schedule table

Say you are building a slide with a conference schedule. Pick a layout with a header row. Type the session names down the first column and the times across the top. If you need one more session at the bottom, click a cell in the last row and press Option-Return.

Next, merge the cells above a group of sessions, such as a morning block, with Control-Command-M. Finish by locking the table with Arrange > Lock. That keeps a stray click from moving the schedule while you present.
Merge cells for headers and titles
A merged cell helps when one header spans several columns. Select the cells you want to join, then press Control-Command-M. To split them again, press Control-Shift-Command-M.
Use merges for headers and titles. Keep the data cells separate, so each row still reads as a row when you edit it later.
Why a table won't edit, move or delete

A locked table cannot be edited, moved or deleted. Apple says locking stops all three actions. If you click a table and nothing changes, check whether it is locked. Select the table, open the Arrange menu, and reverse the lock.

Apple's cell-content guide gives the same advice for adding content. If you cannot add content to a table, reverse the lock first. Lock the table again when you finish, so a stray drag cannot move it during a rehearsal.
Move cells into a new table

Sometimes a block of cells belongs in its own table. Click and hold the selection until it lifts, then drag it to the new spot. Apple says this moves the cells rather than copying them, so the original spot empties.
Press Command-Z right after a move if it went wrong, before you edit anything else. Undo is simplest when it is the very next action.
Insert a table in Keynote for iCloud

Keynote on iCloud.com has its own table button, and the steps differ a little. Open the presentation in Safari on the latest macOS, because Apple says Keynote on iCloud.com works best there. Then click the Table button in the toolbar and choose a preset layout.

Apple says the presets are designed to match the current theme, so the table should fit the look of the slide. After you add it, use the Table, Cell and Data tabs at the top of the Format sidebar to change it.

Two limits to know. Apple Intelligence features such as Writing Tools and Image Playground are not available in the browser version. Unsupported transitions also appear as Dissolve, so check your transitions before you present.
Mistakes people make with tables in Keynote

items: Looking for an Insert menu. Apple's current Mac guide uses the toolbar button and shows no Insert menu path for tables.
Guessing a shortcut. Apple's shortcut list has no entry for Insert Table or Insert Chart, and Option-Command-T is not on it.
Using Shift-Command-V to add a table. Apple lists that shortcut for inserting a file and for pasting a formula result in tables.
Trying to move the table by one of its cells. Grab the Table handle in the top-left corner instead.
Forgetting that someone else locked the table. Open the Arrange menu and reverse the lock before you give up on it.

blocks.text: If a shortcut does nothing, your keyboard may use a different setting than Apple's defaults. Apple's list shows the defaults. Check whether another app or your keyboard settings use the same keys.
Which Keynote version and plan you need
The steps above come from Apple's guide for Keynote 15.4. If your toolbar says Table instead, follow the same steps. Apple's 13.1 guide describes the same process with the older button name.

Creator Studio is Apple's paid subscription for these apps. MacRumors reports a US price of $12.99 per month or $129 per year. Its paid features include professionally designed themes, the Content Hub, and AI image generation and editing. Tables are not on that list, so you do not need a subscription to add one.
What to do after the table is in place

Play the slide once, so you see the table the way your audience will. If the table holds numbers, check each figure against your source before the talk. Keep edits small once you have started presenting, because a late change is easy to miss.
When the table is right, add notes for yourself on the same slide. The [presenter notes guide](/how-to/add-presenter-notes-in-keynote) walks through that step.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to insert a table in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that Apple documents. Apple's Keynote keyboard shortcuts list has no entry for Insert Table or Insert Chart, and Option-Command-T is not on it. Use the Insert Table or Chart button in the toolbar.

faq.question: Where is the Insert menu option for tables in Keynote?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac guide does not show an Insert menu path for tables. A secondary blog describes one, but Apple's pages do not. Start with the toolbar button.

faq.question: Why does my toolbar say Table instead of Insert Table or Chart?
faq.answer: Apple's guide for Keynote 13.1 calls the button Table. The guide for Keynote 15.4 uses Insert Table or Chart. Check your version under Keynote > About Keynote. The steps are the same either way.

faq.question: Can I insert a table in Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the presentation in Safari on the latest macOS, click the Table button in the toolbar, then choose a preset layout. Apple says the presets are designed to match the current theme.

faq.question: Do I need a Creator Studio subscription to add a table?
faq.answer: The sources do not list tables as a paid feature. MacRumors lists Creator Studio's paid features as themes, the Content Hub, AI image generation and editing, and iCloud collaboration on files up to 4GB. The US price is $12.99 per month or $129 per year.

faq.question: How do I delete a table without deleting the rest of the slide?
faq.answer: Click the table, click the Table handle in its top-left corner, and press Delete. Clicking a single cell and pressing Delete only clears that cell's text.

faq.question: Why won't my table let me type or move it?
faq.answer: The table is probably locked. Select it, open the Arrange menu, and reverse the lock. Apple says locking stops the table from being edited, moved or deleted.

faq.question: Does Keynote 15.4 run on older Macs?
faq.answer: The App Store listing says the current Keynote update requires macOS 26.0 or later. TidBITS reports that Keynote 15.4 raised the requirement to macOS 26 Tahoe. On an older Mac, follow the Apple guide for the version your system supports.

steps.name: Select the slide
steps.text: Open your presentation in Keynote and select the slide where the table goes. Click the slide in the slide navigator on the left so it is active.
steps.tip: Make sure the right slide is selected before you add the table.

steps.name: Click Insert Table or Chart
steps.text: In the toolbar above the slide, click the Insert Table or Chart button.
steps.tip: On Keynote 13.1 the same button is labeled Table.

steps.name: Choose Tables
steps.text: Click Tables. The Add Table pane opens with left and right arrows for browsing the layouts.

steps.name: Pick a layout
steps.text: Browse the layouts with the arrows. Select a table to add it to the slide, or drag it onto the slide where you want it.
steps.tip: Dragging places the table exactly where you want it, so you skip a move later.

steps.name: Type in a cell
steps.text: Click an empty cell and type. To change text that is already there, double-click the cell to place the insertion point.
steps.tip: If typing does nothing, the table may be locked. Check the Arrange menu for the lock command.

steps.name: Move the table
steps.text: Click the table, then drag the Table handle in its top-left corner to move it anywhere on the slide.
steps.tip: The Table handle appears when the table is selected.

steps.name: Resize the table
steps.text: Click the table, click the Table handle, then drag the white square in the bottom-right corner. Hold Shift to keep the proportions.
steps.tip: Without Shift, the width and height change separately.

steps.name: Add a row or column
steps.text: Select a cell, then press Option-Return to add a row at the bottom. Hold Option and press an arrow key to add a row or column next to the selected cells.
steps.tip: Tab adds a column on the right when the cursor is in the rightmost column.

steps.name: Lock the table when finished
steps.text: When the layout is final, select the table and choose Arrange > Lock. A locked table cannot be edited, moved or deleted.
steps.tip: Reverse the lock from the Arrange menu before you make changes again.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't find Insert Table or Chart in the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Check your version under Keynote > About Keynote. Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26.0 or later. On an older guide the button is labeled Table, so look for that.

troubleshooting.problem: Typing does nothing in a cell
troubleshooting.fix: The table may be locked. Select the table, open the Arrange menu, and reverse the lock, then click the cell again.
Check for a lock first. Then select the table and drag the Table handle in its top-left corner, not a single cell.
Apple's shortcut list does not include a table shortcut. Use the Insert Table or Chart button in the toolbar.

troubleshooting.problem: Resizing stretches the table out of shape
troubleshooting.fix: Hold Shift while you drag the white square in the bottom-right corner to keep the proportions.

troubleshooting.problem: Cells moved, and the old spot is now empty
troubleshooting.fix: Moving cells leaves the original spot empty, because Apple says the cells move rather than copy. Press Command-Z right after the move to undo it.
